projects.title: Spiking Patch Selection for Event-Based Visual Odometry
projects.role: Master's Thesis | University of Paderborn | Grade 1.0
projects.description: Can a spiking neural network replace the CNN that decides which image patches DEVO tracks? I trained SNN patch selectors with two temporal encodings and compared them with CNN baselines in 150 visual-odometry runs on MVSEC, UZH-FPV and held-out TartanEvents sequences. Also built TartanEvents (1.3 TB) and, as an extension, a SLAM back-end that runs end to end.
metrics: Both SNNs beat both CNNs on held-out TartanEvents
features: SNN-based patch selection for event-based visual odometry
SNN patch selector (LIF neurons, surrogate gradients) inside DEVO; all geometry left unchanged for a like-for-like comparison
Integration with the DEVO visual odometry pipeline
Two encodings: replayed voxel grid (T = 4) and time-surface frames (T = 8)
Benchmarking on MVSEC, UZH-FPV and held-out TartanEvents sequences (150 evaluation runs)
Held-out TartanEvents: both viable SNN variants beat both CNN baselines on both sequences
Ablation: a learned score scale hurts; the time-surface encoding is the most robust
Analysis of accuracy under fast motion; latency on neuromorphic hardware identified as future work
TartanEvents: all TartanAir RGB sequences (30 environments) converted to events with vid2e (1.3 TB), publicly released
Extension, SuperEventSLAM: keyframes, SuperEvent features, three-stage loop verification and g2o pose-graph optimization; the full pipeline runs end to end at 36.7 FPS
Extension status: loop verification is not yet reliable (untuned thresholds), so drift is not reduced yet; tuning and a ground-truth audit are next steps
Own Python visualisation library on Pangolin for live tracking, mapping and loop closures

media.caption: Visual-odometry accuracy (ATE, cm, mean over 10 runs; lower is better). The spiking selectors are blue and orange: best on MVSEC and held-out TartanEvents; on fast UZH-FPV motion the DEVO-pretrained CNN, trained on upsampled events, is still best.
SLAM extension (SuperEventSLAM) running end to end: event frame, map and trajectory, feature matches and loop verification. 30 s, sped up.
